verdicts.title: Counting lifts of Brauer characters
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper we examine the behavior of lifts of Brauer characters in p-solvable groups where p is an odd prime. In the main result, we show that if φ\in IBrp(G) is a Brauer character of a solvable group such that φhas an abelian vertex subgroup Q, then the number of lifts of φin Irr(G) is at most |Q|. In order to accomplish this, we develop several results about lifts of Brauer characters in p-solvable groups that were previously only known to be true in the case of groups of odd order.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses counting lifts of Brauer characters in p-solvable groups, bounded by abelian vertex subgroup order |Q|, with no mention of Boolean formulas, Frege proof complexity, or Brauer groups associated with formulas.

verdicts.title: Finite simple characteristic quotients of the free group of rank 2
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper we describe how to explicitly construct infinitely many finite simple groups as characteristic quotients of the rank 2 free group $F_2$. This shows that a "baby" version of the Wiegold conjecture fails for $F_2$, and provides counterexamples to two conjectures in the theory of noncongruence subgroups of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. verdicts.title: Brauer spaces for commutative rings and structured ring spectra
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Using an analogy between the Brauer groups in algebra and the Whitehead groups in topology, we first use methods of algebraic K-theory to give a natural definition of Brauer spectra for commutative rings, such that their homotopy groups are given by the Brauer group, the Picard group and the group of units. Then, in the context of structured ring spectra, the same idea leads to two-fold non-connected deloopings of the spectra of units.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Brauer spectra for commutative rings and structured ring spectra via algebraic K-theory, with no mention of Boolean formulas, Frege proof systems, or proof complexity. It shares only the 'Brauer group' vocabulary with the conjecture.
